Devices Dealers Blog About Studios OnomatoPedal Merch EarthQuaker Devices Info Email Search Menu EarthQuaker Devices Info Email Search Devices Dealers Blog About Studios OnomatoPedal Merch Barrows Barrows® Fuzz Attacker Please enable your browserís JS to load this productís data. Barrows pays homage to the iconic MKII circuit while adding modern refinements that would make even the most discerning vintage purist weep tears of harmonic joy. At its heart, Barrows features a trio of carefully matched germanium transistors nestled within finely tuned circuitry that has been lovingly coaxed to produce everything from light, singing distortion to crushing fuzz tones with nearly infinite harmonic-rich sustain. The phase-corrected and buffered output ensures it plays nice with other pedals down the line, while the increased output volume and wide range of fuzz tones make it a versatile sonic weapon. All this power is packed into a compact footprint that saves precious real estate on your pedalboard. This isn’t just another fuzz box – it’s a portal to the fabled tones that have haunted the dreams of fuzz fanatics for decades.         Controls     Level: Controls the output volume of Barrows. Unity gain sits around noon, but you’ll find plenty of volume boost available when you need to push your amplifier into blissful submission. Attack: This is where the magic happens. At lower settings, Barrows provides singing, amp-like distortion with superb touch sensitivity. As you rotate clockwise, the circuit transforms into an increasingly aggressive fuzz monster, building to crushing, sustain-drenched tones that seem to go on forever. The wide range of this control means you can find everything from gentle breakup to full-on sonic annihilation. Power This device takes a standard 9 volt DC power supply with a 2.1mm negative center barrel. We always recommend pedal-specific, transformer-isolated wall-wart power supplies or multiple isolated-output supplies. Pedals will make extra noise if there is ripple or unclean power. Switching-type power supplies, daisy chains and non-pedal specific power supplies do not filter dirty power as well and let through unwanted noise. DO NOT RUN AT HIGHER VOLTAGES! EarthQuaker Devices browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal browse by enclosure mini pedal EarthQuaker Devices Barrows - Fuzz Published on September 25, 2025 EarthQuaker Devices fuzz mini pedal pedal Black Silver Explosion Black Silver Black Silver Explosion Black Silver Black Silver Explosion Black Silver Cult FX Edition Cult FX Edition custom custom Information Barrows by EarthQuaker Devices is a modern fuzz pedal designed by Jamie Stillman that reinterprets the classic Tone Bender MkII circuit with contemporary improvements for reliability and versatility. At its core, the pedal features three carefully matched germanium transistors within a precisely tuned circuit capable of producing everything from light, amp-like distortion to dense, sustaining fuzz tones. It retains the MKII's defining characteristics of cutting, mid-focused presence, authoritative low end, and bright upper-frequency grind while eliminating the inconsistencies of vintage units. Several updates distinguish Barrows from traditional MKII designs. A phase-corrected buffered output ensures compatibility with other pedals in the signal chain, and expanded output volume allows the pedal to drive amplifiers or effects with ease. The Attack control provides a wide sweep, enabling tones that range from smooth, touch-sensitive breakup to heavily saturated fuzz. Responsive to both guitar volume adjustments and playing dynamics, Barrows interacts closely with the player's technique. Practical design choices further adapt the pedal for modern use. Barrows runs on standard 9V DC power, removing the need for battery-only operation or positive-ground supplies. Mechanical true bypass switching ensures signal integrity, while its compact enclosure allows it to fit easily on crowded pedalboards. Each unit is hand-assembled in Akron, Ohio. Artwork by Dave Neeson. Controls Level : Sets the output volume. Unity gain occurs around noon, with additional boost available for driving amplifiers or pedals. Attack : Adjusts the character and intensity of the fuzz. Lower settings provide smoother, amp-like distortion, while higher settings produce aggressive fuzz with long sustain.
